source: Chronicling America (via loc.gov — legacy API confirmed dead; used ?fo=json + tile.loc.gov ALTO)

ny_result.coverage_gap: Every NY result is an NYC-metro paper; LOC holds NO Clinton County / Plattsburgh title in range (the correct archive is NYS Historic Newspapers — gated, see nys-historic-newspapers.json).
wrong_men_found: New-York Daily Tribune 1863-11-06 p.8: 'W. L. Hubbell, 17th Conn, captured July 1, at Gettysburg.' (17th Connecticut — not Alexander)

New-York Daily Tribune 1863-11-06 p.8: 'Lieut. F. A. Hubbell, 67th Penn. captured June 15 at Winchester.' (67th Pennsylvania; initials F.A. adjacent to A.F. but wrong regiment/rank/state — not Alexander)

iowa_result.coverage_gap: County filter location_county:pocahontas|location_state:iowa returned total 0 — LOC holds NO Pocahontas County, Iowa paper. A Fonda obituary cannot exist here; the Fonda Times is not digitized in any reachable archive.
iowa_result.namesake_noise: All Iowa 'Hubbell' OCR co-occurrences resolve to FREDERICK M. HUBBELL, the Des Moines millionaire/financier (Terrace Hill; Glucose Sugar Refining Co.; daughter Beulah Hubbell's 1899 wedding to Count Wachtmeister). This is the source of the 1899-dated Iowa 'Hubbell' hits — relevant because it could otherwise be misread as supporting an 1899 death.

same_town_namesake_check.F. M. Hubbell: Des Moines financier — accounts for ALL Iowa newspaper 'Hubbell' noise incl. 1899 hits. Rule out for any Iowa newspaper attribution.
same_town_namesake_check.Julius O. Hubbell: Clinton County NY surveyor (1860s) — relevant for NY papers; could not be screened against NYS Historic Newspapers (gated).

ocr_notes: Moderate garbling ('Get:iy rg' for Gettysburg); surname 'Hubbell' itself OCR'd cleanly in every hit. C8 OCR penalty not decisive here because no candidate was the target anyway.
claude_reasoning: No candidate matched Alexander. NY hits are wrong-regiment Hubbells (R2). Iowa hits are the F. M. Hubbell namesake. The correct archives for him (NYS Historic Newspapers for the wartime honor; the Fonda Times for the obituary) are gated or undigitized — handoffs.
